title: skills: objectstack-data lifecycle rule teaches the sealed-expiry scope and floor PR #37605 ships
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① (the `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line of PR #37605, Part of #31908; claim amendment 7193137455) · Source: fleet (contract review records on PR #37605, the skills follow-up paragraphs of rounds 1, 5 and 6)

## What happens

`skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` teaches `retention` beside `seal`, tenant-scoped `retention_overrides`, and that the sweeper deletes sealed rows. After PR #37605 merges that is true only of some sealed objects. An agent that writes a sealed object from this page will expect an override to shorten the window, and will not know that a packaged sealed object's rows expire by whole signed checkpoints.

`skills/**` is governed (Tier H), and PR #37605 declares a `(narrowing)` arm, so this text does not ride the code PR. It is the second PR of #31908's claim.

## Expected

The page gains, in the wording PR #37605's texts use:

- [ ] **The floor rule:** on a sealed object with no `archive` whose lifecycle is declared in packaged metadata, a retention override below the declared window is rejected, and the declared window applies. To keep rows for less time, shorten the declared window.
- [ ] **The scope:** signed expiry covers objects whose lifecycle is declared in packaged metadata; any other sealed object keeps the row-cutoff retention sweep (seat reading 7212989029 on #31908).
- [ ] **For those other objects, the sentence the page carries today**, kept for that case only: the sweeper deletes sealed rows, which then read as missing.
- [ ] Paid for in the same file or bundle under the token ratchet; no ceiling moves.

Written against the merged #37605 tree.
